title: Football transfer rumours: Rúben Neves next to join Manchester City?
trail: Loris Karius to Besiktas? | Julian Weigl to Manchester City? | Tammy Abraham to Aston Villa?
body: You find us in exuberant, bloodthirsty mood, refreshed and relaxed following a bracing weekend spent gadding around in Leicestershire in a reenactment of the Battle of Bosworth Field that was enjoyed by all involved … until they felt the cold steel of the Mill’s rondel pierce their flesh and send them screaming into The Afterlife. A mobile on-site greasy spoon run by former astronaut Buzz Aldrin, it sells bacon, egg and sausage rolls at extremely competitive rates. In potentially more true news, Liverpool could trim a couple of fringe players from their squad before the European transfer window shuts. The Liverpool Echo says Borussia Dortmund are interested in taking Divock Origi off their hands, following the failure of Wolves to bring him to Molineux earlier this summer. Liverpool are willing to sell, but apparently not for a penny less than £27m. In need of a fresh start, Loris Karius has been told he can leave Anfield and the beleaguered goalkeeper is quite literally talking Turkey with Besiktas. Wolves fans are unlikely to be impressed with speculation – however idle – linking star midfielder Rúben Neves with a £60m January move to Manchester City, who are clearly crying out for some extra creativity in a squad that already includes Kevin De Bruyne, Riyad Mahrez, David Silva, Bernardo Silva, Phil Foden, Leroy Sané, Raheem Sterling and Ilkay Gündogan. City are also reported to be interested in adding 22-year-old Borussia Dortmund midfielder Julian Weigl to their stockpile, but will have to fend off interest from Paris Saint-Germain. Chelsea striker Tammy Abraham could be off to Aston Villa on loan, but the Midlands club are worried he may prefer a move to Italy or the Netherlands. With so many of the club’s players still on holiday after the World Cup, Abraham featured prominently in Chelsea’s pre-season campaign, but wasn’t part of the first-team squad for Saturday’s win over Arsenal. Villa are also hoping to give Liverpool winger Sheyi Ojo and Southampton full-back Matt Targett some minutes in the muck and nettles of the Championship. However, Ojo has caught the eye of Middlesbrough manager Tony Pulis, who is also interested in taking Yannick Bolasie and Muhamed Besic off Everton’s hands. Real Madrid are in the market for a striker and are sounding out the possibility of bringing PSG’s Edinson Cavani, Bayern Munich’s Robert Lewandowski or Lyon’s Mariano to the Spanish capital. The European champions embarked on La Liga life without Cristiano Ronaldo on Sunday night, beating Getafe in front of 48,446 spectators, the smallest crowd to watch a league match at the Bernebéu in a decade. Of course with August being the month when most Spanish folk abandon the cities for assorted summer retreats, there’s no need for Real suits to hit the big red panic button just yet. And finally, following their dismal failure to qualify for the World Cup in Russia, the USA are still looking for a head coach. Dave Sarachan is the man in temporary charge, but could be asked to step down and make way for David Moyes. Meanwhile in China, the owners of Tianjin Quanjian are hoping Rafael Benítez will swap the north-east of one country for that of another by replacing Paulo Sousa as manager of their Super League club when his contract with Newcastle expires in nine months.
